proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(\delta_n\equiv\delta_0\in(0,\infty)\), and abbreviate
\[
D_0(x)=1+(\delta_0-1)e(x)=1-e(x)+\delta_0e(x).
\]
Because \(0<e(x)\leq 1\) and \(\delta_0>0\),
\[
D_0(x)\geq \min\{1,\delta_0\}>0.
\]
Thus every division below is valid.  By \(\textnormal{def:incremental-intervention}\) and the definition \(\tau=\mu_1-\mu_0\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
\psi_{\delta_0}(P)
&=E_P\!\left[\mu_0(X)+\frac{\delta_0e(X)\{\mu_1(X)-\mu_0(X)\}}{D_0(X)}\right]\\
&=E_P\!\left[
\frac{\mu_0(X)D_0(X)+\delta_0e(X)\mu_1(X)-\delta_0e(X)\mu_0(X)}{D_0(X)}
\right]\\
&=E_P\!\left[
\frac{\delta_0e(X)\mu_1(X)+\{1-e(X)\}\mu_0(X)}{\delta_0e(X)+1-e(X)}
\right].
\end{aligned}
\]
This is exactly the point-treatment incremental propensity-score mean at odds multiplier \(\delta_0\) in Kennedy's notation \cite[Corollary~2]{Kennedy2019Incremental}.

Specializing \(\textnormal{def:oracle-score}\) gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\phi_{\delta_0}(O)
={}&\frac{\delta_0A}{D_0(X)}\{Y-\mu_1(X)\}
+\frac{1-A}{D_0(X)}\{Y-\mu_0(X)\}\\
&+\frac{\delta_0\{A-e(X)\}}{D_0(X)^2}\{\mu_1(X)-\mu_0(X)\}
+\frac{\delta_0e(X)\mu_1(X)+\{1-e(X)\}\mu_0(X)}{D_0(X)}
-\psi_{\delta_0}(P).
\end{aligned}
\]
We verify directly that this is the efficient influence function, so the comparison does not rest only on matching notation.  Let \(\{P_t:|t|<t_*\}\) be an arbitrary regular dominated one-dimensional submodel through \(P=P_0\), with score \(S\in L_0^2(P)\).  A dominated submodel preserves \(P\)-null treatment strata.  Differentiating the defining conditional integrals on strata having positive conditional probability gives
\[
\dot e(X)=E_P[\{A-e(X)\}S\mid X],
\qquad
\dot\mu_a(X)=E_P[\{Y-\mu_a(X)\}S\mid A=a,X].
\]
On a null arm stratum the corresponding product \(e\dot\mu_1\) or \((1-e)\dot\mu_0\) is interpreted as zero; here \(e>0\), and the only possible boundary is \(e=1\), where \((1-e)\dot\mu_0=0\).  Boundedness of \(Y,\mu_0,\mu_1\) and the lower bound on \(D_0\) justify differentiation and all subsequent expectations by Cauchy--Schwarz.

For
\[
F(e,\mu_0,\mu_1)=\frac{\delta_0e\mu_1+(1-e)\mu_0}{1-e+\delta_0e},
\]
ordinary differentiation yields
\[
\frac{\partial F}{\partial\mu_1}=\frac{\delta_0e}{D_0},
\qquad
\frac{\partial F}{\partial\mu_0}=\frac{1-e}{D_0},
\qquad
\frac{\partial F}{\partial e}=\frac{\delta_0(\mu_1-\mu_0)}{D_0^2}.
\]
The last equality follows equation by equation from
\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac{\partial F}{\partial e}
&=\frac{(\delta_0\mu_1-\mu_0)D_0-(\delta_0-1)\{\delta_0e\mu_1+(1-e)\mu_0\}}{D_0^2}\\
&=\frac{\delta_0(\mu_1-\mu_0)}{D_0^2}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The marginal law of \(X\) contributes \(E_P[(F-\psi_{\delta_0})S]\).  The three conditional-law contributions satisfy, by iterated expectation,
\[
\begin{aligned}
E_P\!\left[\frac{\delta_0e}{D_0}\dot\mu_1\right]
&=E_P\!\left[\frac{\delta_0A}{D_0}(Y-\mu_1)S\right],\\
E_P\!\left[\frac{1-e}{D_0}\dot\mu_0\right]
&=E_P\!\left[\frac{1-A}{D_0}(Y-\mu_0)S\right],\\
E_P\!\left[\frac{\delta_0(\mu_1-\mu_0)}{D_0^2}\dot e\right]
&=E_P\!\left[\frac{\delta_0(\mu_1-\mu_0)(A-e)}{D_0^2}S\right].
\end{aligned}
\]
Adding these four terms proves
\[
\left.\frac{d}{dt}\psi_{\delta_0}(P_t)\right|_{t=0}
=E_P[\phi_{\delta_0}(O)S(O)].
\]
Each residual term has conditional mean zero, the propensity-path term has conditional mean zero because \(E_P[A-e(X)\mid X]=0\), and \(E_P[F]=\psi_{\delta_0}(P)\); hence \(E_P[\phi_{\delta_0}]=0\).  The outcome envelope and \(D_0\geq\min\{1,\delta_0\}\) also imply \(\phi_{\delta_0}\in L^2(P)\).  For completeness, the tangent space of the unrestricted dominated observed-data model is \(L_0^2(P)\): if \(S\) is bounded and mean zero, then \(dP_t=(1+tS)dP\) is a dominated submodel for \(|t|<\|S\|_\infty^{-1}\) and has score \(S\); for arbitrary \(S\in L_0^2(P)\), its truncated and recentered versions
\[
S_M=\max\{-M,\min(S,M)\}-E_P[\max\{-M,\min(S,M)\}]
\]
are bounded mean-zero scores and converge to \(S\) in \(L^2(P)\).  Thus the tangent-space closure is \(L_0^2(P)\).  The displayed derivative identity for every regular score therefore makes \(\phi_{\delta_0}\) its canonical gradient, hence its efficient influence function.  The assumed condition \(E_P[\phi_{\delta_0}^2]\in(0,\infty)\) makes the resulting Gaussian standardization nondegenerate.  The displayed canonical gradient is the same fixed-multiplier formula reported by Kennedy \cite[Corollary~2]{Kennedy2019Incremental}.

Finally, substituting \(\delta_n=\delta_0\) into \(\textnormal{def:branchwise-intervals}\) gives
\[
C_n^{\mathrm G}(\gamma)
=\left[
\widehat\psi_{\delta_0}
-z_{1-\gamma/2}\frac{\widehat\sigma_{\delta_0}}{\sqrt n},
\widehat\psi_{\delta_0}
+z_{1-\gamma/2}\frac{\widehat\sigma_{\delta_0}}{\sqrt n}
\right],
\]
where \(\widehat\sigma_{\delta_0}\) is the empirical standard deviation of the fitted uncentered version of the same score.  The singleton \(\{\delta_0\}\) is compact, so this is precisely the pointwise, one-multiplier specialization of the fixed-compact Gaussian Wald procedure.  This final assertion is an equality of procedures; coverage requires the separate consistency and central-limit hypotheses and is not being inferred from the variance condition alone.
